title: Resource
description:
One physical or logical thing, from a transceiver to a rack. Deliberately ONE polymorphic entity rather than a table per kind: the alternative is thirty near-identical schemas whose shared fields drift, and a query that cannot ask 'what is in this rack' without a union across all of them.

Containment is the primary relationship (`parent_id`), following OpenConfig's insight that a physical inventory is a tree before it is anything else. A transceiver's parent is a cage, whose parent is a switch, whose parent is a rack. Every other relation -- ports, links, cooling paths -- hangs off that tree.

What a resource IS lives on its ResourceType. What makes it THIS one lives in `identifiers[]`.

resource_type_id.description: The catalog entry this is an instance of. Required: a resource whose type is unknown cannot be power-budgeted, cooled, cabled or validated, so admitting one would only defer the problem.

parent_id.description: The resource physically containing this one. Null only for a top-level resource, in practice a site. A cycle here is invalid; the schema cannot express that, so `backend/contracts/validate.py` checks it.

name.description: The name operators use. For a compute node this is the hostname, because that is what appears in every log, every Slurm queue and every escalation. Not unique by itself -- two sites may both have `gpu-001`.

identifiers.description:
Every known real-world name for this resource. Reconciliation matches on ANY member, which is what lets a record built from a packing list (SERIAL) merge with the same unit discovered over the fabric (IB_GUID) once one system reports both.

Empty is legal but weak: a resource with no identifiers can never be reconciled with a discovered one, so an inventory built entirely without them will duplicate itself on first discovery.

location_id.description: Where it is. Usually set only on rack-level and above, with everything inside inheriting through `parent_id` -- storing a full location on every transceiver is denormalization that goes stale the first time a tray moves.

domain_id.description: The logical grouping this participates in: a compute domain, an IB fabric, an NVLink domain, a power zone.

part_location.description: Position within the parent. This plus `parent_id` is the full physical address, so no path syntax needs inventing.

quantity.description: For consumables tracked in bulk rather than individually -- a bag of quick-disconnect gaskets. Anything with a serial should be its own record instead; a quantity above one means identity was given up, and it cannot be recovered later.

attributes.description: Instance facts the model does not cover: a firmware version, a BIOS setting, a measured coolant flow. Type-level facts belong on ResourceType instead -- putting them here copies them onto every unit and guarantees they disagree.
